changes.text: Campaign filters now decide what Lurkloot farms, not just what the Drops list shows. Two new settings control farming — “Farm campaigns without a linked account” and “Farm campaigns that require a subscription”, both on by default — while the Drops list keeps its own show/hide chips. Anything being farmed always stays visible in the list.
Added a dedicated Diagnostics view with full English detail on what Lurkloot is doing, and the popup now warns you when the extension has critically failed instead of silently going idle.
Added a header button in the popup that jumps straight to your Twitch or Kick inventory page.
Twitch and Kick now run independently, so a slowdown on one platform no longer delays farming on the other.
Farming now pauses automatically when you close a platform's watch tab, and a new watch tab gets a short grace period before it's judged unhealthy.
The activity log can be copied directly from the popup, and diagnostics are recorded by default.
Drops cards in the popup stay collapsed unless their campaign is actively farming, keeping the list easier to scan.
Fixed Twitch and Kick getting stuck on “Checking your signed-in session…” in the popup when an unrelated part of a refresh failed.
Campaigns no longer disappear from the popup when Twitch or Kick briefly fails to respond — your known campaigns and progress are kept until a successful refresh replaces them.
Finished and expired Kick campaigns now show up again, so the “Visible campaigns” settings work the same way on Kick as they do on Twitch.
Fixed Kick's ad detection and Twitch's playback priming occasionally stealing focus from the tab you were watching.

Fixed several Twitch drop-claiming edge cases: tiers that share a campaign benefit, benefits reused across drops with a different award window, campaigns dropping out of view during a scheduler tick, and reward progress not being trusted when it should be.

Fixed Twitch's anti-bot integrity checks sometimes leaving farming stuck after a rejected request, including recovering rejected tokens across retries and avoiding repeated unnecessary verification work.
Fixed automation toggles in the popup not responding promptly, and platform sign-in status not resolving as quickly as it should.

Lurkloot now tracks your Twitch and Kick sign-in status, shows each platform's authentication health in the popup, and automatically pauses farming when you are signed out or blocked so it can resume cleanly once access is restored.
Added Turkish language support, with translation refinements contributed by @canpaksoyyyyyyy-code — thank you!
Added a factory reset action in Settings to restore all preferences to their defaults.
Settings changes now apply immediately without pausing automation.
Stabilized Kick page-context tabs so they no longer get stuck in a bad state during farming.
Fixed Twitch tabless farming falling back to muted watch tabs because required heartbeat services could not be reached.

Expanded Twitch and Kick site access so farming keeps working when either platform moves features between its own services. Your browser may ask you to approve the updated access after installing this update.
Reorganized Settings to make options easier to navigate, and refreshed the footer attribution links.
Renamed “Watch Queue” to “Idle Watchlist” to make its purpose clearer.
Settings now migrate more reliably between version upgrades, preserving your preferences as configuration evolves.
Added automatic claiming for completed Kick daily challenges, with separate per-platform controls for Kick challenges and Twitch channel points.
Lurkloot now avoids farming rewards that cannot be completed before their deadline, with an adjustable safety margin.
Twitch now starts progressing toward the next reward sooner after a claim instead of waiting for the next scheduled cycle.
Compatibility settings now show what each option actually resolves to, grouped by platform, and say whether a value came from the selected profile or a manual override.
Long option names in settings dropdowns no longer squeeze setting titles into several lines.
Added rotating tips in the popup that point to useful settings and shortcuts, with an option to hide them.
Added Twitch and Kick compatibility profiles that keep farming working as those sites change — selected automatically, or manually with expert overrides.
Exporting session credentials for the command-line app now confirms inline in the popup instead of through a browser dialog.
Lurkloot’s source code is now public under the Apache License 2.0.
Added a command-line app that farms drops headlessly — no browser tab or extension required.
The command-line app ships as a Docker image, so you can run it on a server or NAS.
Redesigned the landing page around the command-line app and the now-public source.
What’s New is now shown as a notice in the popup after meaningful updates instead of opening a browser tab automatically.
Activity now shows localized farming events separately from diagnostic logs, with paged history for easier review.
Selected category lists now show category artwork when available.
Twitch now ignores subscription, purchase, and other non-watch rewards when choosing campaigns to farm.
Twitch campaigns no longer appear as “Not linked” when Twitch does not provide a genuine external account-link flow.
Twitch now confirms that a selected live channel offers the intended campaign when that information is available.
Renamed to Lurkloot.
Streamer and channel names are now clickable links to their channel page — in the watch queue, on each drop's allowed channels, and in the automation view.
Added direct links to each drop's campaign page, plus a “No category” grouping for uncategorized drops.
Added a Chrome Web Store link in the settings footer.
Added a link to the Lurkloot website in the popup footer.
Added a What’s New page that opens automatically after meaningful updates.
Clicking the campaign being farmed now jumps straight to its card on the Drops tab.
Activity and Settings sub-pages now show a single back button instead of the full toolbar.
Added an occasional one-time prompt to rate the extension.
Stopped the “no earnable drops left” notification from repeating every minute.
Fixed a tab-close race that could overwrite in-progress farming state.
Added a “Priority list only” farming mode.
Added per-platform category filters and campaign visibility controls.
Added a per-level activity log control and a reset for excluded campaigns.
Added campaign lifecycle pills and a start countdown for upcoming campaigns.
Localized the interface and store assets.
Tabless background farming is now enabled by default.
Reorganized settings into collapsible, grouped sections with a platform switcher.
Kick now tries a background fetch before falling back to a page.
Fixed Kick reward images by resolving relative paths to the Kick CDN.
Fixed editing automation settings while farming was paused.
Fixed the Twitch live-status check so it no longer stalls on a channel that has gone offline.
Hardened Kick drop auto-claim against the live API so claims register reliably.
More reliable Twitch drop claiming by replaying the page's Client-Integrity token.
First public release: automatic Twitch and Kick drop farming through your own logged-in session.
Opt-in tabless low-resource mode that farms without a visible video tab.
Automatic drop claiming, including Twitch channel points.
Activity log panel with adjustable detail levels.
Smart channel switching and real campaign progress tracking.
Detect already-owned Twitch drops to avoid re-farming them.
